intro: Searching for a quantity surveyor near me usually means a building project is moving from an idea into real money — a renovation, an extension, a self-build or a contract that has gone off track. You want someone local who can estimate and control construction costs, prepare tender documents and manage payments and variations as the work unfolds. We can introduce you to a suitable UK quantity surveyor in your area, who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a local quantity surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most enquiries come from people who need cost clarity before or during building work, close enough to visit the site.
needs: You are planning an extension or renovation and want early cost advice so the budget does not run away before work starts.
You have builders' tenders in front of you and need help comparing them fairly and understanding what each price actually covers.
You are self-building and want someone to prepare tender documents and keep an eye on contract payments as stages complete.
A final account has become a dispute with your builder and you need an independent view of variations and what is genuinely owed.
You are buying or commissioning work and want a local professional who can visit the site and talk through costs face to face.
context_heading: Why local matters, and how to check who you are dealing with
context: A quantity surveyor near you can visit the property, see the site conditions and meet you and your builder in person, which is often more practical for cost advice, tender comparisons and sorting out a disputed final account. Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process; chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS.

You can check the RICS directory yourself and ask which report or service type you are getting before you commit. It is also worth confirming in writing what the quote covers, since quantity surveying fees are usually price on application and depend on the scope and size of your project.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the project — for example an extension, a renovation, a self-build or a final account dispute — and roughly how far along it is.
Say where the property is, so we can introduce a quantity surveyor who covers your area.
Explain what you need most: early cost advice, help comparing tenders, preparing tender documents, managing payments or resolving a final account.
Mention whether drawings, a specification or builders' quotes already exist, as this shapes what the surveyor will need to do.
Note any deadlines you are working towards, such as a tender return or a contract stage, without needing exact dates.
Include the best way to reach you and any times you are available for a site visit or call.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the quantity surveyor
questions: What will your fee cover for my project, and how will it be calculated?
Are you a member of RICS, and is your firm RICS-regulated?
Will you visit the site, and how often during the work?
Can you help me compare builders' tenders and explain the differences between them?
How will you handle variations and payments as the work progresses?
If we end up disputing the final account, how would you approach it?

faqs.q: What does a quantity surveyor actually do on a home project?
faqs.a: Quantity surveyors estimate and control construction costs, prepare tender documents and manage contract payments and variations. On a home project that can mean advising on a realistic budget early, comparing builders' tenders and helping settle the final account.

faqs.q: How do I find a quantity surveyor near me?
faqs.a: You can tell us your project and location and we will introduce you to a suitable UK quantity surveyor who covers your area, who will quote you directly. You can also check the RICS directory to see who is local and whether they are chartered.

faqs.q: When should I bring in a quantity surveyor?
faqs.a: Early cost advice prevents overspend, so it is often worth involving one before you commit to a budget or appoint a builder. They are also useful later for comparing tenders and for disputes over final accounts.

Fees are price on application, because the cost depends on the scope and size of your project and the service you need. Ask the surveyor to set out in writing what the quote covers before you proceed.
